title: Day Trading: Your Dollars at Risk
summary: Regulator warning: day traders typically suffer severe early losses, depend on margin, face high costs, and should distrust claims of easy profits and non-objective seminars.

assertions.quote: Day traders typically suffer severe financial losses in their first months of trading, and many never graduate to profit-making status.
Day traders also have high expenses, paying their firms large amounts in commissions, for training, and for computers.
This is why many day traders lose all their money and may end up in debt as well.
an author of a publication about day trading stands to profit if you start day trading
If the firm does not know, or will not tell you, think twice about the risks you take in the face of ignorance.

verdicts.note: EU CFD brokers must publish client loss percentages, typically seventy to eighty percent; US stock and options brokers have no such requirement.

ESMA had to mandate that each CFD provider publish the percentage of its retail accounts that lost money over the past 12 months, implying such disclosure was not standard; applies to EU CFD providers.
Regulators such as the SEC and CVM provide information about day-trading risks but not the actual odds, and the strong public reaction to the study suggests retail day traders were unaware of them.

The FCA proposed requiring UK CFD firms to disclose the share of client accounts in profit or loss, implying they did not; but it notes the US CFTC already requires retail forex dealers to publish that figure each quarter.

assertions.quote: Some websites have sought to profit from day traders by offering them hot tips and stock picks for a fee.
